task: Design analogies for this concept, for the lesson that follows the junk-filter lesson.
concept: weight: how much one clue counts towards a decision. In the junk filter, an urgent word counts 3 points and an exclamation mark 1. In training, the weights are adjusted using many labelled examples instead of being set by hand.
lessonContext: Learners may have done 'How does a junk filter decide?': a filter adds up clues into a score and compares it with a threshold; a deeper layer says real filters work out their points from many examples (training).

audience.label: School learners, classes 8-12
audience.pacing: short loops; visible response within 1 second; mini-cycle within 3 minutes
audience.gamification: light: challenges and takeaways; no points, streaks or leaderboards

existingAnalogies.source: an exam with a pass mark
existingAnalogies.breakPoint: An examiner reads and understands your answers. The filter only counts clues.
